The number of countries that have legalized same-sex marriage has grown over time, which is why different sources report different figures. According to Our World in Data, by 2022 same-sex marriage was legal in 32 countries, and with Andorra, Estonia, and Greece joining, the total reached 35 [d4]. The Human Rights Campaign reports 37 countries where same-sex marriage is currently legal [d1], while Equaldex puts the figure at 38 countries [d3]. Older sources give lower counts: the Council on Foreign Relations cited 33 countries [d6], a 2017 Pew Research article referred to "more than two dozen" [d2], and one source reported only 24 nations [d8], reflecting an earlier snapshot. CNN notes that Thailand's legalization would add to a list of "more than 30 countries and territories globally" [d5]. The discrepancies across sources are best explained by the fact that more countries have legalized same-sex marriage over time, making older figures outdated; the most current estimates from credible sources place the number between 35 and 38 [d4][d1][d3].
